programme: HDAC3 and SIN3A are class-I-HDAC-associated transcriptional corepressors sitting over a Treg/anti-inflammatory gene set (FOXP3, IL10, CTLA4, IL2RA, IFNG, LTA via MSC; STAT3, SOCS3, TGFBR2 via SIN3A), while MAZ and SSRP1 control a parallel vascular/barrier-remodeling gene set (MMP1, MMP9, MMP14, VEGFA, NOS3 via MAZ; NOTCH3, TGFB1, TIMP1, ADAMTS7, PTGS2 via SSRP1) — an epigenetically-gated circuit coupling immune tolerance to vessel and epithelial barrier integrity.
role_in_a: In IBS, this axis would sit at the gut mucosal/stress interface: histone-acetylation changes upstream of visceral hypersensitivity, together with Treg/IL10-type tolerance signalling and MMP-driven remodeling of gut barrier and vasculature, fit the low-grade mucosal immune dysregulation described in stress-associated and post-infectious IBS.
role_in_b: In stroke, the same class of factors maps onto HDAC-driven microglial neuroinflammation, NOTCH3/MMP-mediated small-vessel and blood-brain-barrier remodeling during ischemia-reperfusion, and Treg-mediated limitation of secondary injury.
shared_axis: Both conditions could reuse one chromatin-corepressor-gated circuit that sets Treg/anti-inflammatory tone and, through it, licenses the matrix-remodeling enzymes that govern epithelial or endothelial barrier integrity — deployed at the gut mucosal barrier under stress/visceral afferent signalling in IBS, and at the cerebrovascular/BBB interface under ischemic stress in stroke.
reasoning: HDAC3 is independently documented in a stress/visceral-hypersensitivity IBS model and in stroke-associated neuroinflammation, and Open Targets separately ranks it high for stroke, so the corepressor arm of the module has real footing in both diseases. But SIN3A, MAZ and SSRP1 have no disease-specific placement beyond their target-gene content and one Open Targets percentile, and no source states an IBS-stroke connection through any of these factors — the shared-axis claim leans on general knowledge of Treg/barrier biology in each disease rather than on what was retrieved.
support: 35600618 — ties HDAC3-associated histone acetylation in the amygdala to stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity, an IBS model; 42677156 — HDAC-targeted lipid-nanoparticle delivery reduces microglia-mediated neuroinflammation after stroke; 42517197 — HDAC modulation (via melatonin/valproic acid) limits oxidative injury in cerebral ischemia.
how_to_falsify: Inhibit or knock down HDAC3 (and separately SIN3A) in a stress-model gut preparation and in a middle-cerebral-artery-occlusion model run in parallel. If the account holds, both should show coordinated shifts in Treg/FOXP3-pathway markers alongside MMP9/NOTCH3/VEGFA expression at the relevant barrier. If HDAC3 loss changes inflammatory tone in one tissue but not the other, or if the Treg-marker and matrix-remodeling genes move independently of each other, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Only 12 patient-group comparisons across 2 independent cohort pairs support these recurrence counts, which caps confidence regardless of literature depth. FOXO3, ETS1, KLF2, EPAS1, DNMT1 and other blood/vascular master regulators were removed as tissue-generic, so no single 'master regulator' story should be expected or reached for here. Ten factors (ATOH7, SATB1, HSF1, MYOCD, etc.) were single-view — top in one patient group only — and are correctly excluded. The two MSC-linked citations (41480397, 42351306) concern mesenchymal-stem-cell therapy, not necessarily the transcription factor MSC/musculin used here — a likely gene-symbol collision in retrieval — so despite the reader's note they are not counted as literature support. DLX3, DLX5, HOXC9, HOXD1, ZNF335, BPTF and PHF5A recur at comparable frequency but carry osteogenic/homeobox-developmental target sets with no route into this programme, and are deliberately left out rather than folded in.
